text: Proposition three is about whether existing higher
income-tax rates should expire.
The additional rates apply to roughly the highest-earning
two percent of taxpayers.
Proposition three would make those higher rates permanent.
The analyst estimates five to fifteen billion dollars
of annual revenue maintained after the scheduled
expiration.
The wide range reflects the volatile incomes and
investment gains of high earners.
A voter might prefer protecting existing revenue for
education and other services,
with the additional tax concentrated on high earners.
A skeptical voter could want the state to
honor the sunset or reduce reliance on a
small, volatile tax base.
Yes makes the current higher rates permanent;
no preserves their scheduled expiration.
